title: Entitlement and Vendor Sourcing Guidelines — Controls, Approvals, and Templates
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This document provides an integrated set of company-wide rules, approval flows, and reusable templates for: access and permissions (entitlements), change management for operational/production systems, data classification and lifecycle, procurement and expenses, vendor sourcing & onboarding, and travel expense controls. It is designed to reduce operational risk, enforce least privilege, and streamline approvals while preserving agility for product and infrastructure teams.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that access company systems or data. This covers cloud resources, internal apps, procurement of goods/services, travel booking and reimbursements, and vendor selection and onboarding.

Principles (Summary)

- Least Privilege: Grant the smallest set of permissions required for a role.
- Separation of Duties: Critical actions (approval, procurement, deployment) should require distinct approvers.
- Risk-Proportional Controls: Higher value or higher-sensitivity items require stronger review (security attestations, SSO integration, contract review).
- Fast Revoke: Access revocation must be processed within 24 hours of offboarding or role change for privileged access.
- Single Source of Truth: Inventory all active entitlements and vendor contracts in the central systems (IAM console / Contract Registry).

1) Access & Permissions (Entitlement Lifecycle)

Overview

Redwood uses role-based access control (RBAC) mapped to documented job roles and product teams. Service accounts, human accounts, and machine-to-machine credentials are treated separately.

Role definitions and ownership

- Role owner: the team lead responsible for defining role duties and membership rules.
- Access approver: usually the manager or team lead of the resource owner.
- IAM steward: Security team engineer that audits roles and entitlement policies quarterly.

Provisioning process (standard requests)

1. Requestor opens an Access Request via the Access Portal (conformance form link: /templates/access-request-form).
2. Automatic validation: system verifies if request matches a defined role template.
3. Manager approval required for standard roles. For privileged roles, extra approvals required (Security + IT Ops).
4. Provisioning executed automatically via IAM automation; manual steps documented in the request.

Temporary access and emergency access

- Temporary access: timeboxed to a maximum of 7 days by default; extensions require the same approval chain and explicit justification.
- Emergency access (break-glass): approved by on-call SRE lead + Security, logged to the Incident Log, and subject to retrospective review within 5 business days.

Deprovisioning and offboarding

- HR offboarding triggers an automated deprovisioning workflow. Privileged credentials must be revoked within 24 hours; all other access within 72 hours.
- Service account keys rotated or revoked within 7 days when an associated owner leaves.

Entitlement audit cadence and metrics

- Quarterly entitlement audit by IAM steward.
- KPIs: % of privileged roles with documented owners, average time to revoke privileged access, number of outstanding orphaned accounts. Target: 100% privileged revocations within 24 hours; orphaned accounts < 0.1% of active accounts.

Approval Matrix (text table)

- Purchase / Contract Approval Matrix:
  | Amount (USD) | Approver(s) | Required Supporting Docs | Legal Review? | Procurement Involvement? |
  |--------------|-------------|-------------------------|---------------|-------------------------|
  | <= 5,000     | Manager     | Business justification   | No            | Optional                |
  | 5,001–50,000 | Dept Head + Procurement | Cost comparison, vendor info | Yes if SLA or data access | Yes |
  | > 50,000     | VP Finance + Procurement + Legal | Contract draft, security attestations | Yes | Mandatory |

2) Change Management (Production-facing)

When to use: Any change that can affect customer-facing services, data integrity, or deployment pipelines.

Change categories

- Standard: pre-authorized low-risk changes (patch updates, config changes within tested ranges).
- Normal: requires RFC, CAB review, scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency: out-of-band changes to mitigate active incidents.

Process (Normal change)

1. Submit RFC: include scope, rollback plan, test plan, monitoring dashboard links, and blast radius analysis.
2. Peer and stakeholder review (developers, SRE, security).
3. CAB approval for medium/high risk changes. CAB meets daily with a rolling agenda; urgent items escalated.
4. Scheduled deployment and post-change monitoring window (minimum 2x expected risk window).
5. Post-change report and lessons learned; small changes may be documented in change log only.

Emergency changes

- Emergency changes require two on-call approvers (SRE + Security) and must be entered into the RFC system within 24 hours for retrospective CAB review.

3) Data Management and Classification

Classification levels

- Public: Safe for public consumption.
- Internal: Company-internal operational information.
- Confidential: Sensitive operational data, PII, internal roadmaps.
- Regulated: Data subject to regulatory controls (GDPR personal data, HIPAA PHI, customer-controlled datasets).

Handling rules (short)

- Regulated data: stored only in approved regions and only when a DPA and technical controls (encryption at rest and in transit, strict ACLs) are in place.
- Confidential: accessible only via RBAC roles; audit logging enabled.
- Retention: default engineering logs 90 days; product telemetry 365 days; financial and legal records 7 years (or as required by law).

Data access requests

- Data access requests follow the same Access Request workflow but must include data justification and retention plan. Approval chain includes Data Owner + Security.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Procurement principles

- Competitive sourcing where feasible for purchases > $25k.
- Use approved vendor lists to accelerate procurement.
- All vendor agreements that process customer or regulated data must include a DPA and acceptable security attestations.

Corporate card and expense policy (high-level)

- Travel must be pre-approved for business need. Use company travel portal for bookings where possible.
- Per diem and allowed expenses summarized: Airfare: economy (upgrades require manager approval). Hotel: up to $200/night in major markets (exceptions by manager). Meals: reasonable and itemized. Personal expenses are disallowed.
- Expense submission: receipts required for all expenses > $25. Electronic receipts submitted via Expense portal within 30 days. Late submissions may be rejected.

Reimbursement turnaround

- Standard reimbursements processed within 10 business days after approval. Exceptions handled by Finance Ops.

5) Vendor Management & Sourcing

Vendor classification and risk tiers

- Tier 1 (High risk): vendors handling regulated data or critical production paths. Requirements: SOC2 Type II or ISO27001, contract with DPA, SLA with financial remedies, penetration test report or attestation.
- Tier 2 (Moderate risk): vendors with limited access to internal systems or noncritical data. Requirements: security questionnaire, basic contract terms, procurement review.
- Tier 3 (Low risk): commodity vendors (office supplies, non-sensitive services). Standard PO process.

Vendor onboarding checklist

1. Business case + cost estimate and approval per matrix.
2. Procurement performs Sourcing Review and initial vendor security questionnaire.
3. Legal reviews contract and DPA if needed.
4. Security performs technical review (SSO integration, IP allowlist, encryption requirements).
5. Finance registers contract in Contract Registry; procurement sets payment terms.

Contracts and SLAs (sample requirements)

- Standard SLA baseline for Tier 1 vendors: 99.9% availability, 2-hour incident acknowledgement, 24-hour incident response window. Financial remedy tiers defined in contract.
- Data processing clause mandatory for any vendor storing or processing regulated or confidential data.

Vendor offboarding

- Offboarding steps: revoke credentials, terminate API keys, confirm data deletion or secure handoff, update Contract Registry, final invoice processing. Security and Procurement must jointly confirm.

6) Travel & Events Controls

Booking and approvals

- All business travel requires manager pre-approval in Travel Portal. Team leads may define conference budgets per headcount.
- International travel must have Travel Risk Assessment completed for the destination.

Expense claim rules (summary)

- Receipts are required for all hotel and airfare bookings. Meals above $75 require itemized justification. Alcohol allowed only for client entertainment with manager approval and separate line-item.

Duty of care and emergencies

- Company provides emergency assistance phone for employees traveling on business. Security team maintains travel watch for high-risk locations.

7) Templates & Reusable Artifacts

- Access Request Form: /templates/access-request-form (fields: requestor, role, justification, expiry).
- Standard Procurement Requisition: /templates/procurement-requisition (fields: cost center, vendor, amount, justification, procurement contact).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (short): /templates/vendor-security-questionnaire.
- Change Request (RFC) Template: /templates/rfc-template (fields: rollback plan, monitoring, blast radius).

Appendix: Example procurement workflow (text flow)

1. Requestor completes Procurement Requisition and attaches vendor quotes.
2. Procurement validates vendor & cost center; if > $25k, run sourcing process.
3. Legal and Security review templates if required.
4. Approval recorded; PO issued.

Enforcement and exceptions

- Policy exception requests submitted to Policy Exceptions Board (peers from Finance, Security, Legal) with documented compensating controls. Exceptions are timeboxed and reviewed quarterly.

Ownership and maintenance

- Document owner: Finance-Legal (owner: Corporate Procurement Manager).
- Security maintains related access and entitlement controls.
- This document will be reviewed annually or earlier when major regulatory or product changes occur.
